messages:
cheng: Heads-up — noticed a small perf regression on the canary fleet tonight. Continuous-batching workloads see queue_time spikes and a corresponding jump in tail latency. Perfetto trace: https://perfetto.example.com/trace/2440012345 :eyes:

cheng: Quick summary of what I pulled from the trace and nsys: the runtime is occasionally choosing the float fallback path for a quantized matmul kernel under specific batch-size/sequence-length combos. That fallback shows ~1.8-2.0ms kernels vs the quantized path ~0.07-0.12ms, and queue_time increases from ~0.6ms -> ~3.0ms in the same windows. :thinking:

cheng: nsys excerpt (trimmed):
```
Time(us)  Kernel                               Duration(ms)
0.000      quant_matmul_fast                    0.09
0.120      cutlass_quantize_postprocess         0.02
0.150      fallback_sgemm                       1.85  <-- spike correlates with queue wait
0.200      queue_wait                           3.10ms (observed)
```

sara: Which commit introduced this? any obvious changes to kernel selection heuristics?

cheng: Looks like commit 2b4a7d9 ('tune prefetch threshold & scheduling heur') modified the prefetch threshold + kernel-selection tie-breaker. The change made the runtime prefer a 'safe' sgemm when predicted tile occupancy was low. Patch diff: `if (tile_fill < 0.2) prefer_fallback = true`

devon: We also saw concurrent KV cache sweeps in the same intervals on those nodes — the sweeper spikes CPU and causes small scheduling jitter which pushes some requests over the 'low occupancy' boundary. I think the prefetch threshold interacts badly with the KV cache timing.

devon: local config snippet that reproduces class of traces: 
```
kvcache:
  sweep_interval_ms: 1000
  prefetch_threshold: 64
batching:
  window_ms: 8
  max_batch: 32
```

maria: I reproduced on my laptop with perfetto. If I disable the kvcache sweeper or bump window_ms to 12ms the fallback rate drops a lot. Here's my perfetto timeline (public): https://perfetto.example.com/trace/2440012401 :thumbsup:

cheng: Good repro. Proposed immediate mitigation for canary: revert the tie-breaker in 2b4a7d9 and reduce kvcache.prefetch_threshold from 64->16 for the next canary wave. Also add an explicit kvcache-sweeper backoff when GPU batch window > 10ms.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: canary rollout started (build 4621)

devon: I'll prepare a quick patch with the revert + config toggle and run nsys perf on 3 nodes.

maria: Also adding a small perf regression test to the nightly harness that simulates concurrent sweeper + continuous batching sequences (we were missing that corner). I can add perfetto markers so traces are easier to filter.

cheng: Plan: (1) devon submits revert PR targeting canary, (2) infra toggles prefetch_threshold=16 for canary, (3) run canary 4621 + collect nsys/perfetto, (4) if tails look good, roll to prod. If not, revert canary and roll forward with additional telemetry flags.

sara: sounds good. @devon can you link the PR here when ready?

devon: will do, aiming for a PR within 1.5h.

cheng: thanks — tagging @oncall in case we see anything weird during rollback.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: build 4621 succeeded on subset, monitoring for 30m

maria: attaching the small trace snippet I used (inline):
```
trace summary:
- fallback rate: 6.4% -> 0.8% after config change
- p50 latency: 12.2ms -> 11.1ms
- p99 latency: 128ms -> 36ms
```

cheng: Nice numbers. Keep the traces coming and please capture host-side CPU (kvcache sweeper), kernel timeline, and request-level kvcache hits. I'll assemble a small postmortem if this surfaces again.

sara: :thumbsup:
